title: Module 4 Interpretation Check
intro: Each item gives you a short research situation. Decide what the evidence supports.

items.q: Anna scored 82 on a test with mean 70 and SD 8. Ben scored 88 on a test with mean 78 and SD 5. Who did better relative to their class?
o: Ben, because his z = 2.00 exceeds Anna's z = 1.50

items.q: Scores on a scale have mean 50 and SD 10 and are normally distributed. About what proportion score below 45?
items.why: z = (45 minus 50)/10 = −0.50. The tail beyond z = 0.50 is .3085.

items.q: A score has z = +1.00. What proportion of a normal distribution scores higher?
items.why: The tail beyond z = 1.00 is .1587. The .84 is the proportion below.

items.q: A student computes z = (60 minus 50)/10 = 1 and says "60 is 1 point above the mean." What is wrong?
o: The z of 1 means one standard deviation, which here is 10 points
The score is below the mean
items.why: Always translate z back to units. One SD equals 10 raw points in this example.

items.q: Which z score is the most unusual in a normal distribution?
items.why: The farther z is from zero in either direction, the smaller the tail area and the more unusual the score.
